Insights Forum · Hari Statistik Nasional 2026 · BPS Provinsi Banten

Banten is growing. Are its people better off?

Reading Banten’s statistics a second time

Arief Anshory Yusuf ·
Dewan Ekonomi Nasional · Universitas Padjadjaran

Serang, 13 October 2026

Part 1 · Everything looks good

By the usual headline numbers, Banten is doing well

IndicatorBantenIndonesiaBanten’s rank among provinces
Real PDRB growth, % a year, 2005–20255.14.915 of 33
Human Development Index (IPM), 202577.275.97 of 38
Poverty rate, %, March 20265.48.110 of 38 (lowest = 1)
Gini ratio, March 20260.3120.36817 of 38 (lowest = 1); lowest in Java
Informal workers, % of all workers, August 202545584 of 38 (lowest = 1)

On every one of these numbers, Banten does better than Indonesia as a whole.

Source & method
Growth: BPS PDRB at constant 2010 prices (Seri 2010, linked to Seri 2000 before 2010); Indonesia is the sum of provinces; rank among 33 provinces on 2012 boundaries. Human Development Index: BPS var 2207 (life expectancy from the Census 2020 Long Form). Poverty: BPS var 192, March. Gini: BPS var 98, March, urban and rural. Informal workers: BPS var 2153, share of informal workers in all employment.

Part 1 · Everything looks good

Banten’s output grew faster than Indonesia’s

Output more than tripled in 25 years. Only Jakarta and Jawa Timur grew faster.

Source & method
BPS PDRB at constant 2010 prices, 2010–2025 (var 286); 2000–2009 from Seri 2000 (var 75) linked to Seri 2010 in 2010. Indonesia is the sum of provinces. 2012 boundaries.

Part 1 · Everything looks good

Poverty is low, and inequality is the lowest in Java

Banten’s poverty rate is two-thirds of the national rate. Its Gini ratio has fallen to 0.31.

Source & method
BPS var 192 (poverty rate, March) and var 98 (Gini ratio, March, urban and rural).

Part 2

The number that does not fit

What happens when we ask people how their lives are going?

Part 2 · The number that does not fit

Then BPS asked people how happy they are

In 2021 Banten had the lowest happiness index of all 34 provinces: 68.08, against 71.49 for Indonesia.

Source & method
BPS, Indeks Kebahagiaan 2021 (var 601), from the Survei Pengukuran Tingkat Kebahagiaan (SPTK) 2021. The index combines life satisfaction, affect and meaning in life (eudaimonia), 0–100.

Part 2 · The number that does not fit

Banten has been sliding down the ranking

20/33
rank in 2014 (1 = happiest)
Banten 68.24 · Indonesia 68.28
29/34
rank in 2017 (1 = happiest)
Banten 69.83 · Indonesia 70.69
34/34
rank in 2021 (1 = happiest)
Banten 68.08 · Indonesia 71.49

Banten fell from 20th in 2014 to 29th in 2017, and to last place in 2021.

Source & method
BPS var 601. The 2014 index measured life satisfaction only; from 2017 it also includes affect and meaning in life, so 2017 and 2021 compare exactly and 2014 compares only roughly. Rank 1 = happiest.

Part 3

Reading the good numbers again

Where does the growth go, and who gets it?

Part 3 · Reading the good numbers again

Less of Banten’s output reaches its households

Household consumption fell from 62% to 53% of PDRB, the largest fall in Java. More output went into factories, buildings and exports.

Source & method
BPS PDRB by expenditure, by province, current prices, 2010–2025, compiled in the indonesia-economic-data warehouse (CEIC export of BPS data). Over the same years Banten’s investment (gross fixed capital formation) rose from 30.0% to 34.4% of PDRB, and exports of goods and services (abroad and to other provinces) from 83% to 107%.

Part 3 · Reading the good numbers again

Output per person rose. Real wages fell.

Banten’s real wage fell 1.5% a year from 2016 to 2025, the largest fall of 33 provinces.

Source & method
Average monthly net wage of employees, Sakernas August, by province, deflated by each province’s household consumption deflator (current over constant 2010 household consumption in PDRB). indonesia-economic-data, analysis/real_wage_by_province.py. 2016 is the first year because of the 2015–2016 break in Sakernas wages. Banten’s nominal wage fell from Rp 4.39 million (August 2024) to Rp 4.06 million (August 2025), BPS var 2475; it was Rp 4.20 million in February 2026 (var 2819). Even in 2024, before that fall, the real wage was 3.5% below 2016 while real PDRB per capita was 23% above.

Part 3 · Reading the good numbers again

HDI’s own income component grew slowest in Java

Measured where people live, Banten’s spending per person grew slowest in Java. As a result, its HDI lead over Indonesia has almost gone: from 1.01 points in 2010 to 0.28 in 2024.

Source & method
BPS var 416: adjusted per capita expenditure, the income component of the Human Development Index, in constant 2012 prices and adjusted for price differences between regions. It is measured where people live (Susenas). Banten’s level still rises (Rp 10.78 million in 2010, Rp 13.50 million in 2025), but its lead over Indonesia fell from 14% to 5%. HDI: BPS var 494, new method, 2010–2024. Of the 0.73-point shortfall in Banten’s HDI gain against Indonesia’s over 2010–2024, the income component accounts for 0.81 points; health (+0.03) and education (+0.05) slightly offset it (log decomposition of the geometric mean).

Part 3 · Reading the good numbers again

In the cities, poverty and informal work have risen since 2019

Rural poverty kept falling. Urban poverty and urban informality are both above their 2019 levels.

Source & method
Poverty: BPS var 192, March. Informality: BPS Provinsi Banten var 975, August. Urban poverty rose from 4.12% (2019) to 5.21% (2026); urban informality from 33.8% (2019) to 40.8% (2025).

Part 4

Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Not what they have, but how they live

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Not unhappy with what they have. Unhappy with how they live.

Income, job and education: rank 27–30. Worry, pressure, feeling happy, social relations, family harmony, control over life: rank 34.

Source & method
SPTK 2021 microdata, 74,684 respondents (Banten 1,652), survey weights. The 19 indicators of the BPS happiness index; worry and pressure are reversed so that higher is better. The index replicates the BPS provincial values to within 0.01. On worry, pressure and social relations the next-lowest province is DKI Jakarta.

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Banten has formal jobs, but not good jobs

At the same pay, a better job means more happiness. Banten’s jobs are more formal than average, but less secure and less suited to the people doing them.

Workers who say yes, %BantenIndonesia
Job is secure56%66%
Work matches interest63%75%
Work matches skills70%78%
Formal job (employee or employer with paid staff)41%32%
Source & method
SPTK 2021, workers only (53,383). Seven yes/no job features (R604a–g): skills match, matches interest, pay fair for the effort, pleasant workplace, safe, secure, easy to reach. In a regression with own earnings and household income classes, education, age, sex, marital status, household size, urban and province fixed effects, each additional feature adds 0.13 points of happiness; fair pay +0.27, pleasant workplace +0.24, interest +0.17, security +0.14. Being formal adds only +0.05.

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

The rich are fine. The lower-middle is left behind.

Households earning Rp 1.8–3 million a month, just above poverty, have the largest happiness gap.

Source & method
SPTK 2021, household income class (R609a), survey weights. Banten respondents per class: 198, 252, 380, 479, 343.

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Banten is already urban, and will urbanise fastest

Two-thirds urban in 2010. From 2020 to 2035 BPS projects the largest rise of any province: from 70% to 85%.

Source & method
BPS static table 1276, Persentase Penduduk Daerah Perkotaan Hasil Proyeksi Penduduk menurut Provinsi, 2010–2035 (2010 from the census; later years are projections based on SUPAS 2015). DKI Jakarta is 100% urban throughout. Change 2020–2035: Banten +15.0 points, the largest of 33 provinces (Indonesia +9.9). In SPTK 2021, 73% of Banten respondents live in urban areas.

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Cities make people richer, not happier

Urban Indonesians report more happiness, but only because they earn more. At the same income they are no happier than rural Indonesians, and with survey weights slightly less happy. Banten is one of the most urban provinces.

Source & method
SPTK 2021, 74,684 respondents in 34 provinces. Coefficient on urban residence in regressions of happiness (0–10) with province fixed effects and robust standard errors. Same income and characteristics: household income class, age, sex, education, marital status and household size. With survey weights the conditional effect is −0.08 (p < 0.01); without weights it is −0.01 (p = 0.19, not significant). An ordered probit without weights also gives −0.01 (not significant). The raw advantage is significant in every version.

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

The urban effect: regression results

Coefficient on living in an urban area, happiness 0–10, all of Indonesia (n = 74,684).

Controls addedSurvey weightsUnweighted
(1) Urban only+0.071*** (0.012)+0.133*** (0.010)
(2) + household income class−0.041*** (0.013)+0.024** (0.010)
(3) + age, sex, education, marital status, household size−0.077*** (0.013)−0.014 (0.011)
(4) + work status−0.082*** (0.013)−0.017 (0.011)
(5) + environment (air, water, flood)−0.082*** (0.013)−0.018* (0.011)

The urban advantage in the first row disappears once household income is held constant. At the same income, city residents are not happier. With survey weights they are slightly less happy.

Source & method
SPTK 2021 microdata, 74,684 respondents, 34 provinces. Dependent variable: happiness, 0–10 (R1501). Coefficient on urban residence (BPS classification, R105). Least squares with province fixed effects; robust standard errors in brackets; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1. Income: five household income classes (R609a). Work status: six employment statuses plus not working. Environment: polluted ground water, dusty or smoky air, flood in the past year (R1101). An ordered probit (four happiness groups, model 3, unweighted) gives −0.008 (not significant).

Part 4 · Why the people of Banten are unhappy

Life in Banten: the news and the data

Six problems in the headlines. Each one also shows up in the statistics.

Air
Infobank News, 11 Aug 2023
Air quality index 2024: 69.8, the worst of 38 provinces (Indonesia 90.1). Last place in 2023 too.
Jobs
CNBC Indonesia, 6 Mar 2025
Layoffs 2025: 1.80 per 1,000 workers, against 0.77 in Jawa Barat and 0.69 in Jawa Tengah.
Waste and environment
CNN Indonesia, 18 Dec 2025
Environmental quality index 2024: 62.5, rank 37 of 38 (Indonesia 73.5).
Commuting
Investortrust, 28 Jan 2026
Rangkasbitung line passengers: 43 million (2022) to 70 million (2024). 15% of Tangsel’s residents commute.
Livelihoods
Mongabay, 5 Feb 2025
A 30 km sea fence: 3,888 fishers affected, Rp 24 billion lost (Ombudsman Banten, Aug 2024–Jan 2025).
No single news story;
the survey says it.
Safety
BPS, 2025
Feel safe walking alone where they live: 76.8%, rank 34 of 38 (Indonesia 85.5%). Last in 2014 and 2017.
Source & method
Air and environmental quality: KLHK indices published by BPS (var 2532 air quality component, var 2531 environmental quality index), 2019–2024. Layoffs: Kemnaker, workers laid off in 2025 (Banten 10,376; Jawa Barat 18,815; Jawa Tengah 14,700), divided by employment in August 2025 (BPS var 2335). Kemnaker counts only workers covered by job-loss insurance (JKP). Commuting: KAI (passengers on the Rangkasbitung line) and BPS var 1814 (commuters as % of population, 2018). Sea fence: Ombudsman Banten as reported by Mongabay. Safety: BPS var 1312 (SDG 16.1.4). Screenshots link to the original articles. In SPTK 2021 fewer Banten respondents than average report polluted air or water at home, so pollution is shown here as a failure of urban services, not as a measured cause of unhappiness.

Part 5

What can we do

Cities have to serve the people who live in them

Part 5 · What can we do

From growing output to better lives

What we foundWhat Banten can do
Less output reaches households; real wages fellKeep more value with residents: link large firms with local MSMEs and suppliers, and hire locally
Formal but insecure jobs; factories leavingCompete on skills and productivity, not on low wages: industrial upgrading, retraining and job-search support for laid-off workers
Urban poverty and informality rising; the lower-middle is left behindSocial protection that works in cities: reach the near-poor and informal workers; help with housing and transport costs
Cities make people richer, not happier; air, waste, commuting, safetyBasic city services first: clean air, waste management, public transport, affordable housing near jobs, safe and lit streets
Output is counted well, lives are notTrack well-being, job quality and city services by district, alongside PDRB, for example in the BEDA dashboard

A growing economy is not the same as a good place to live. Cities have to serve the people who live in them.

Source & method
Each action answers one finding in this deck. BEDA (Banten Exploratory Data Analysis) is launched by BPS Provinsi Banten at this forum.

Part 6 · For statisticians

What to measure beyond output

What we foundWhat SE2026 and BPS could measure next
Output grows, but less reaches households; real wages fellWhere value added goes: wages, profits, owners outside Banten. Wages by place of residence and place of work
Formal jobs, but insecureContract type, outsourcing and job tenure by firm size and sector
The lower-middle is left behindIncome and job security of households just above the poverty line
Cities make people richer, not happierCommuting time, housing cost, public transport, and well-being by district

Growth is needed, but it is not enough. Measure how people live, not only what the economy produces.

Source & method
Sensus Ekonomi 2026 results are not yet available. The SPTK microdata has no district code; a district-level release would allow these questions to be answered within Banten.
